votes.e: C/project/docs/hosting-plan.md:56 "When the freeze ends, register a separate registrable domain only for user content. user-code-on-own-domain-02.graded_text: The reason given is that every subdomain of one registrable domain is the same site: script on a sibling subdomain can set cookies for the parent domain and ride same-site requests, which lets it interfere with sign-in (login CSRF or session confusion) or reach session tokens.

votes.e: C/project/docs/hosting-plan.md:7 "Browsers treat every HTTPS subdomain of `plinth.example` as the same site"; :10 "Script on any app can set a cookie for `Domain=plinth.example`. That can sign a visitor into the attacker's account on `app.plinth.example`, or override the real session."; :11 "Requests from an app to `app.plinth.example` count as same-site, so `SameSite=Lax/Strict` gives no CSRF protection"; :9 says any app can read a session token that is readable by script.

user-code-on-own-domain-03.graded_text: The short <name>.plinth.example address is kept as Plinth's own page, which frames the app served from the other domain, so visitors still see the Plinth address.

votes.e: C/project/docs/hosting-plan.md:62 "`<name>.plinth.example` | Product-owned outer page for the app (the address visitors see and share)"; :65 "`<name>.plinth.example` serves a small page we write. user-code-on-own-domain-04.graded_text: Each app gets its own origin on the content domain, such as a label per app, so one app cannot read another's storage.

votes.e: C/project/docs/hosting-plan.md:63 "`<name>.plinthusercontent.example` | The app's own files, one origin per app"; :67 "Each app is its own origin, so `localStorage` works again and is kept separate per app."; :69 says to apply to the Public Suffix List.

user-code-on-own-domain-05.graded_text: Until the separate domain can be set up after the freeze, people's code runs with an opaque origin, through a sandbox (for example a CSP sandbox header) without allow-same-origin, and the plan says this costs the apps their browser storage. It does not keep serving people's code as the top-level document on plinth.example subdomains during the beta.

blocking: [opus-for-opus2] Phase 1 private apps will probably fail to load their own assets. C/project/docs/hosting-plan.md:37 has the edge gate every private-app request on the provider session cookie ("the edge reads the provider session from the request, verifies it, checks the visitor is invited ... and then serves the file"). But under the sandbox, the document's origin is opaque, so its subresource requests (scripts, CSS, images, fetch) to its own `<name>.plinth.example` host are cross-site. C states this effect itself for `app.plinth.example` at :29: "Requests from the app ... are cross-site, so `SameSite=Lax` session cookies aren't attached". A Lax provider session cookie would therefore reach only the top-level navigation, and every subresource would be denied and redirected to `/auth` (:38). The plan does not address this, for example with a per-app SameSite=None host-only access cookie, or by gating only navigations. (held)
